import boto3
from braket.aws import AwsDevice
from braket.circuits import Circuit
from braket.devices import Devices

device = AwsDevice(Devices.Amazon.SV1)

bell = Circuit().h(0).cnot(0, 1)
task = device.run(bell, shots=100)
print(task.result().measurement_counts)

sim_check.substitution: device = LocalSimulator() instead of AwsDevice(Devices.Amazon.SV1); the test imports LocalSimulator and does not import boto3 or AwsDevice.
sim_check.notes: The README sample targets SV1, Amazon Braket's simulator. LocalSimulator was used so the run did not need an AWS account. Shot counts are sampled.

snippet.code:
> from qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider import FakeBelemV2
> backend = FakeBelemV2()
> estimator = Estimator(backend)
>
> # Convert to an ISA circuit and layout-mapped observables.
>
> pm = generate_preset_pass_manager(backend=backend, optimization_level=1)
> isa_circuit = pm.run(qc)
> mapped_observables = [
>     observable.apply_layout(isa_circuit.layout) for observable in observables
> ]
>
> job = estimator.run([(isa_circuit, mapped_observables)])
> result = job.result()
>
> # This is the result of the entire submission. You submitted one Pub,
> # so this contains one inner result (and some metadata of its own).
>
> job_result = job.result()
>
> # This is the result from our single pub, which had five observables,
> # so contains information on all five.
>
> pub_result = job.result()[0]

sim_check.substitution: The documented simulator block already uses FakeBelemV2. The Markdown source prefixes each line with '> '. The test removed only those prefixes and defined qc and observables from the earlier cells on the same page. QiskitRuntimeService was not called.
sim_check.notes: The page pins qiskit-ibm-runtime~=0.47.0. This run used 0.50.0, which still provides FakeBelemV2 and Estimator(backend). qiskit-aer was installed because Estimator.run on FakeBelemV2 requires it. No IBM account was used.

snippet.code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit_ionq import IonQProvider

provider = IonQProvider()
simulator_backend = provider.get_backend("simulator")

# Create a basic Bell State circuit:
qc = QuantumCircuit(2, name="IonQ Qiskit guide - simulator example")
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

# Run the circuit on IonQ's platform:
job = simulator_backend.run(qc, shots=10000)

# Print the counts
print(job.get_counts())

sim_check.output_excerpt: IonQCredentialsError: Credentials `token` may not be None!
sim_check.notes: IonQProvider() constructs without a token, and get_backend('simulator') returns. simulator_backend.run then raises IonQCredentialsError. The page says the job runs on IonQ's platform. No account was created and no token was supplied.

gaps.why: https://www.fujitsu.com/global/about/research/technology/quantum/ and https://global.fujitsu/en-global returned Too Many Requests. The fetches were not retried.
gaps.would_need: An official Fujitsu cloud page that names the device offered today and its access tier.

gaps.why: The fetched xanadu.ai page is a JavaScript shell and does not name a cloud QPU or a tier. https://cloud.xanadu.ai/ did not resolve.
gaps.would_need: Xanadu cloud documentation that names a QPU available today and states the access tier.

gaps.why: The fetched Quandela cloud page does not name a specific QPU as available today and does not state an access tier.
gaps.would_need: A Quandela device list that marks a named QPU available and states the tier.

gaps.why: The fetched qcs.rigetti.com page does not name a QPU. PyQuil docs say programs can run on QCS but do not name the current devices. Rigetti QPUs are recorded here only where Braket or Azure name them.
gaps.would_need: A Rigetti QCS page that lists the QPUs accepting jobs and states the access tier.

gaps.why: The AQT products page says ARNICA is remote access to IBEX quantum computers and does not state a tier. The IBEX device Braket lists is recorded on Amazon Braket, where a price is published.
gaps.would_need: An ARNICA pricing or signup page that states the access tier for IBEX.

gaps.why: The Chinese cloud homepage offers Origin Wukong and describes free real-machine time to claim. The fetched Origin pages do not state a headquarters address, so this file does not define the operator or a route.
gaps.would_need: An official address for the operator, plus the ordinary access terms for the physical machine.

gaps.why: Pasqal's QPU page names Google Cloud, Azure, OVHCloud, and Scaleway. Azure's tier is recorded from Microsoft's pricing page. The fetched Pasqal pages do not state the access tier on Google Cloud, OVHCloud, or Scaleway.
gaps.would_need: A Pasqal or host-cloud page that states the tier for FRESNEL on Google Cloud, OVHCloud, and Scaleway.

gaps.why: Superstaq documents a Sqale QPU target and says a Superstaq API key can be obtained from superstaq.infleqtion.com. The fetched pages do not say whether that key is free, paid, or approved.
